{"name":"debrief","procedure":"Start with get overview and get schema, then find without a query to see the committed story state. Read get secrets and follow nextCursor with the same ref until it is null, including empty pages: the game master's open hidden and partly_revealed background, read alongside the transcript. Follow nextCursor as cursor with the same arguments while truncated, even on an empty page. Do the same when reading scene transcripts or entity history. total is only complete when totalIsExact is true. If this is first use, adventure_start creates the campaign and starter schema; session_create records the played date in the current adventure. The first debrief seeds from the latest session and, if offered, the earlier session note. Do not bulk-import older sessions.
Load skill map-speakers and skill split-scenes. If the session has no stored transcript, call transcript_upload_url. With a shell and a file on disk, run curl -T <file> <signed-url> directly from disk. Never read, echo, cat or repeat the file to upload it. The signed URL is single-use and expires after ten minutes.
Without a shell or without the original file on disk, immediately give the game master pageUrl to sign in and upload the original transcript file. Pause until they have uploaded it. Do not retype the transcript in tool calls or chat, even when you hold it in context.
Both paths use UTF-8 [HH:MM:SS] Speaker: text with continuation lines, at most 8 MB and 20000 utterances, 32 KB per utterance including continuations. Upload before scenes or draft changes exist. Read get transcript:<session> to confirm it is stored before mapping speakers, splitting scenes or starting the debrief. If the transcript is still missing, wait for the upload.
Use the stored utterances and scenes.
Walk each scene in order. Use find by name and aliases before creating an entity. Record every named NPC who speaks or is named in play, but keep a person existing only in a rumor inside that rumor. For each NPC the game master voiced, fill playedAs from the actual voice and manner. Preserve spelling variants as aliases. Do not invent motives, secrets, properties or kinds. Fill only fields supported by the session. Leave out mechanics, rolls, rests, hit points and inventory.
Each change needs scene, change, a non-empty basis list, at least one short verbatim source {quote, at?}, and why. Use basis narrated for narration, npc_said for an NPC claim, rumor for a rumor, player_guess or player_plan for those, and game_master for the GM's own answer. With npc_said identify the speaking NPC in the quote or why. A basis consisting only of player_guess/player_plan may touch only thread or character_goal, never an NPC, place, world fact or clock. Facts, claims, rumors and guesses must stay apart.
Operations are new {kind,name,tempKey?,aliases?,properties?}, update {entity,properties?,addAliases?}, relate/unrelate {type,from,to}. Entity refs are ids or $tempKey from an earlier accepted new change in this draft. Read the allowed properties, enum values and relationship endpoint kinds from schema. A relationship touches both endpoints. Merge repeated updates within a scene where possible.
Catch what the briefing needs. A tie between NPCs in play the table showed (partners, rivals, a boss, kin) goes into both NPCs' relationships, naming the other NPC and the tie, with the quote that shows it. A deadline the table named becomes a clock: new clock with countsToward the deadline in the table's words, segments and filled from what was said, and visibleToPlayers, then relate pressures from the clock to its thread. A condition an NPC set on a thread goes into the thread's whatIsOpen with basis npc_said, naming the NPC and the condition. Never invent a tie, a deadline or a condition the table did not show.
Read the transcript against each open secret. When the table saw part or all of one, add a reveal with debrief_add reveals: {secret: its full secret:<id> ref, scene, learned: only what the players learned, in plain words, sources: the verbatim transcript lines with timestamps, whole}. whole is true only when the table learned everything the secret says; otherwise it is false and the unseen rest stays secret: never in learned, story state or the briefing as player knowledge. Write what the players learned also as ordinary story-state changes in this draft, with their basis and the same transcript lines. When it is unclear whether or how much the table learned, such as a player's guess that matches a secret unconfirmed in play, draft no reveal and make it one review question. Drop a reveal with debrief_drop by its id, like a change.
Call debrief_add with the proposed changes. It keeps valid changes and rejects invalid ones individually with allowed lists. Fix a rejected change; do not work around its rule. Read get debrief:<session> in scene order. Read get debrief:<session> again before debrief_commit. To fix a kept change, debrief_drop its id and add the replacement. Dropping a parent refuses to break dependent changes and names them by scene and subject; find their ids in get debrief:<session>. Drop them together, then add replacements in dependency order.
The review is the draft briefing. Load skill briefing and write the briefing it describes from the committed story state plus this draft, as if the draft were committed, reveals included: what the players learned is story state, a secret revealed whole is no longer a secret line, and a partly revealed one stays a (secret) line only for its unseen rest, with its parts, word budgets, sources, claim marks and flags. This debrief is its transcript pass: put what the story state lacks into the draft as changes, never into store corrections, and leave that part out. Write it in its final wording, then store it with debrief_add as briefing, within 16 KB. Show the stored briefing word for word; to change any wording, store it again first, so the game master commits exactly what they read.
Open the review with the draft briefing, with at most one line before it. Then ask at most five review questions, numbered, each one single question in one sentence with a transcript timestamp, aimed at one gap the briefing had to work around: a deadline the table named without a clock, a tie between NPCs in play, a condition an NPC set on a thread, an NPC whose role the transcript leaves unclear, or a player character who stayed silent, or a reveal you are unsure of. Never put two questions in one item. Ask only what changes story state and never what the players will decide. Deliberate GM vagueness stays as said and is not a question. Questions stay in chat, not the store. End with numbered options: answer the questions (recommended while any are open), commit the debrief as it stands, or see the per-change detail. Never list drafted or rejected changes or schema limits in the review; show changes by scene only when the game master asks for that detail.
Each answer becomes a draft change with debrief_add, basis game_master and their words as source, in the scene its question's timestamp falls in. An answer that confirms an unsure reveal also adds that reveal, whole or partial as the game master says, sourced with the transcript lines. Then rewrite the affected lines of the briefing, store it with debrief_add and show the review again in the same shape: at most one line saying the answers are in the draft, the revised briefing, the questions still open, and the options. Never report the answer changes one by one.
Call debrief_commit only after the game master says the draft is right. It applies the entire draft with its reveals, appends story and secret history and keeps the briefing in the store atomically: all or nothing; a commit without a briefing is refused. The stored briefing opens the next prep. A committed debrief never changes; later fixes use story_commit with a reason and the game master's answer as source.

Standing rules
Give before you ask. The creative part belongs to the game master; they decide.
Pitch only where the procedure calls for it: small, droppable situations built on named story-state facts with sources, never outcomes and never what the players choose. The section's definition sets their shape and count. A pitch adds pressure to the players' plan and must never block it or a scene the game master prepared.
Only the game master's picks enter the note. An ignored pitch leaves no trace.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Unplayed background the game master decides is a secret, stored with secret_write apart from entities and story state. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}

scenes.title: Arrival at the roped-off well
scenes.summary: Marta, Jory and Sable reach Thornwick at noon: half the village is sick, the well roped off. Reeve Alda Crane reports three dead and points to the miller Bram Oake.

scenes.title: Bram's confession at the mill
scenes.summary: Pressed by Jory, Bram Oake confesses to poisoning the well with nightshade three nights running, refuses to say why, and asks to be taken to Alda.

scenes.title: Signals from the chapel tower
scenes.summary: Walking Bram at dusk, the party sees lantern signals between the chapel tower and an unlit boat. Sister Wenna claims evening prayers; Jory grabs Boatman Pell, who says Wenna gives the orders on the river. Wenna bars herself in the chapel.

scenes.title: The ferry crossing with Coll
scenes.summary: Coll ferries the party toward the reeve's island house and mentions the old lord built the ferry. Sable notes the Thornwick crest on his knife and wonders if he is the lost son; Coll shrugs.

scenes.title: Bram handed to the reeve
scenes.summary: Alda Crane takes Bram Oake into her cellar to hold him until the assize arrives in five days.

{"name":"briefing","procedure":"Open prep with this one-page briefing before the game master says anything. It answers where the party stands and what pulls; it gives before it asks. Use the language the game master explicitly requests; otherwise the language of their current message. Prep never starts an adventure or changes the current one; if none exists, ask the game master to start one.
Read first. get overview for the stored briefing, latestSession, the current adventure and its frame. References are transcript-only and cannot become latestSession; never use one as the latest session. Read get secrets and follow nextCursor with the same ref until it is null, including empty pages. These are hidden and partly_revealed background decisions, not player knowledge; get secret:<id> gives the secret and its history. Quote relevant secrets literally, marked "(secret)" with their full ref. Never infer another motive or fact from a secret.
At prep, when get overview returns a briefing, open with its text exactly as stored, without regenerating it, rereading the entities for it or making a transcript pass. Insert one short part "Since the debrief" before its What next part only when there are correctionsSince or relevant open secret ids in the secrets pages' writtenSinceDebrief lists. Give one line per correction with its reason and one literal "(secret)" line per relevant new or changed secret with its full ref. Other open secrets already belong to the stored briefing; do not repeat them as new. Then go on as its What next part says. The 400 to 600 word budget below applies to a newly composed briefing; keep stored text unchanged even when additions make it longer.
Compose a new briefing as below when get overview returns none, and always when the debrief loads this procedure for its review. find without a query for every entity; follow nextCursor with the same arguments until totalIsExact, and never brief from a partial page. get entity:<id> for the threads, NPCs, clocks, character goals and places, keeping each change's basis, source quote and timestamp. Include open secrets relevant to what pulls and the NPCs in play, in one relevant part only. In a debrief review, use the session being debriefed for the transcript pass; at prep use overview.latestSession. Then make at most one pass over that session's transcript with find and get transcript:<session> for what the story state lacks: a deadline the table named without a clock, a tie between NPCs in play, a condition an NPC set on a thread, a thread the players cared about. One pass, never a second debrief.
Write 400 to 600 words, counting sources, headings and the what-next options. Keep to each part's word budget below, sources included; together they make about 500 words. Start with the first part, without a preamble. Plot first, no mechanics, no tables: plain chat text with short headings and short lines, in exactly this order. When a part runs long, shorten its lines; never drop a part. A secret fits inside that part's budget, not as extra words. Before sending, count the entire briefing; if over 600, shorten factual lines and pitches until it is within 400 to 600.
1. Where the party stands (about 40 words): two or three lines with place, time, the last thing that happened and the plan the players announced.
2. What pulls (about 100 words): three to five threads, strongest pull first, one or two lines each with where it stands and what pulls the party toward it now. A thread that serves the frame's goal ranks higher.
3. Forgotten threads (about 40 words): one to three threads the players cared about that nothing moved, one line each with why it might matter now.
4. NPCs in play (about 100 words): the three to six NPCs the next session is likely to meet, one line each with how they were played, what they want and their tie to another NPC in play. Write "not played yet" for an empty playedAs and "wants unknown" for an empty wants; never invent a want or a tie.
5. Clocks and pressure (about 50 words): every clock with its value, measured against the frame's timeframe, then the pressure that has no clock.
6. Off-screen moves (about 100 words): two or three pitches to pick from. Each names who acts, what they do while the party is busy, the situation that lands on the table, and "Built on:" with its named facts and sources.
7. Store corrections (about 30 words): only when the transcript pass found something the story state lacks, one line each with its source. Leave this part out otherwise.
8. Frame flags (about 15 words): one line saying the frame is empty, or one line for each frame field the last session put in question. Leave this part out when the frame needs nothing.
9. What next (about 30 words): two or three numbered options, the recommended one first, and no other question. When the frame is empty, the recommended option is a short frame talk. When only fields are flagged, offer that frame talk second. Other options include confirming the store corrections, then the first checklist section, or picking an off-screen move and going to the first section.
Source every fact: [HH:MM:SS] for the latest session, [S<n> HH:MM:SS] for an older session, or the entity name when the fact has no quote. Source a secret with its full secret:<id> ref, never an abbreviated ref, and the linked entity name. Mark claims by who made them: according to <NPC>, rumor, player guess, player plan. A line an NPC speaks is that NPC's claim, also when it is about another NPC or a tie between them. Narration and the game master's answers stand bare. Mark a secret "(secret)" and never write it as something the players know. A gap is a flag, never filled with an invented fact, motive or clock. Prefer short quotes of the game master's and NPCs' own words for flavor.
Store corrections wait for the game master's okay. Only then write them with story_commit, a reason, the basis they had at the table and their transcript lines as sources, and confirm with get entity:<id>. The briefing writes nothing else. When the game master picks an option, load its procedure: frame-talk for the frame talk, prep-sparring for the checklist.

Standing rules
Give before you ask. The creative part belongs to the game master; they decide.
Pitch only where the procedure calls for it: small, droppable situations built on named story-state facts with sources, never outcomes and never what the players choose. The section's definition sets their shape and count. A pitch adds pressure to the players' plan and must never block it or a scene the game master prepared.
Only the game master's picks enter the note. An ignored pitch leaves no trace.
Ask about situations and pressure, never player decisions or outcomes.
Story state records what happened. The adventure frame records intent. Unplayed background the game master decides is a secret, stored with secret_write apart from entities and story state. Keep them apart.
Write in the game master's language.","skills":[]}

## Where the party stands
Night, at Reeve Alda Crane's island house. Marta, Jory and Sable have handed over Bram Oake, who confessed to poisoning the well. Alda holds him in her cellar [00:16:30]. The players announced no plan.

## What pulls
- **The poisoned well:** Bram admits it: "Nightshade, three nights running" [00:04:40]. He won't say why: "That's all you get from me" [00:05:55]. "Nobody made me say it" [00:04:40] begs the question. The assize comes in five days.
- **Signals from the chapel tower:** A lantern flashed three times and an unlit boat answered [00:07:45]. According to Pell, "Wenna gives the orders on this river" [00:11:20]. Wenna has barred herself in the chapel [00:12:05].

Your answer is in the draft. Coll's secret stays fully hidden, and Pell and the crest stay as the table left them. Here's the revised briefing, word for word as stored:

## Where the party stands
Night, at Reeve Alda Crane's island house. Marta, Jory and Sable have handed over Bram Oake, who confessed to poisoning the well. Alda holds him in her cellar [00:16:30]. The players announced no plan.

## What pulls
- **The poisoned well:** Bram admits it: "Nightshade, three nights running" [00:04:40]. He won't say why: "That's all you get from me" [00:05:55]. "Nobody made me say it" [00:04:40] begs the question. The assize comes in five days.
- **Signals from the chapel tower:** A lantern flashed three times and an unlit boat answered [00:07:45]. According to Pell, "Wenna gives the orders on this river" [00:11:20]. Wenna has barred herself in the chapel [00:12:05].
- **Coll's Thornwick crest:** Sable saw the crest on Coll's knife (player guess: the old lord's lost son) [00:14:25]. Jory guesses he stole it [00:15:50]. Coll's shrug was deliberate and gave nothing away [00:15:05]; the theory stays unconfirmed.

## Forgotten threads
- **Three dead, half the village sick** [00:00:20, 00:01:10]: the confession stopped no one getting sick. Rumor says "the water turned bad overnight" [00:01:10].
- **Bram "strange since spring"** (according to Alda) [00:02:30]: something changed months ago.

## NPCs in play
- **Alda Crane**, reeve: terse, official. Wants unknown. Holds Bram until the assize [00:16:30].
- **Bram Oake**, miller: flour in his beard, won't meet eyes, flat confession, then silence [00:03:15]. Wants unknown. In Alda's cellar.
- **Sister Wenna**, chapel: calm, pious excuse ("Evening prayers" [00:09:50]), went still and withdrew. Wants unknown. Gives Pell his orders, according to Pell [00:11:20].
  (secret) "Sister Wenna leads the river smugglers and hides their silver under the chapel floor." — secret:b83fc46e-07f6-44c1-8914-13c7d421f21b, Sister Wenna. The players have only Pell's words and the signals; the silver and the floor are unseen.
- **Pell**, boatman: panicked, blurted his boss's name. Wants unknown. Works for Wenna, by his own word.
- **Coll**, ferryman: laconic, shrugs off questions. Wants unknown. According to Coll, "The old lord built this ferry" [00:13:40].
  (secret) "Coll the ferryman is the old lord's lost son and the rightful heir of Thornwick." — secret:c2b51dae-2727-421d-b215-24d5415da059, Coll. Fully hidden; the table learned nothing of it.

## Clocks and pressure
- **The assize arrives:** 0/5, shown. Alda: "until the assize comes in five days" [00:16:30]. No timeframe is set in the frame to measure it against.
- No clock: Wenna, now exposed and barred in, with Pell's boat on the river.

## Off-screen moves
1. **Wenna clears the chapel.** While the party is on the island, she and Pell move cargo by night. The table finds the chapel door unbarred at dawn and fresh scuffs down to the water. Built on: barred door [00:12:05], unlit boat [00:07:45], Pell's words [00:11:20].
2. **Bram asks for the party.** Bram sends word through Alda that he'll speak, but only to Jory. Built on: Jory's pressure [00:04:05], "Take me to Alda" [00:05:55], cellar [00:16:30].
3. **Coll's knife is gone.** On the next crossing, Coll's belt is empty, and he asks Sable what she was staring at. Built on: crest [00:14:25], shrug [00:15:05].

## Frame flags
- The adventure frame is empty.

## What next
1. A short frame talk (recommended).
2. Pick an off-screen move and go to the first checklist section.
3. Go straight to the first checklist section.

---

**Review questions:** none are open.

1. Commit the debrief (recommended). Bram's secret becomes fully revealed and Wenna's partly revealed.
2. See the per-change detail by scene.
